relevance_note: Single-patient case report of a germline TNFAIP3 variant: 'Whole exome sequencing identified a heterozygous de novo pathogenic variant of the TNFAIP3 gene (c. 1777 C>T in exon 7, p.Q593X)'.
method_note: Read the full paper manually; it has no tables, and Figure 1 data (IgG, anti-dsDNA, CD19 over time) are not available as text, so nothing was transcribed by script. A Python script in the scratch directory only assembled the JSON and checked spans and fields. Individuals: the patient is labelled 'patient' (single unnamed patient). The paper says WES was done on 'this patient and both parents' and that neither parent carries the variant; the parents are not labelled individually, so they are recorded as 'parent 1' and 'parent 2' (constructed labels, sex not assigned) with no clinical data. The maternal and paternal grandmothers are mentioned only to explain consanguinity and have no clinical or genetic data, so they have no rows. Contradictions/inconsistencies: (1) the case description says MMF was discontinued after the hospitalization at age 11, whereas the Discussion says she 'had last received rituximab and mycophenolate at age 10 years'; (2) onset of recurrent infections is given as 'At the age of 12' (and ages 12–14 in the case description) but also 'At age 14, she began experiencing recurrent infections'; both onsets are recorded on separate rows. The age at which WES was done (and hence age at genetic diagnosis) is not stated (referral to a genetic counselor at age 14; symptoms 'in the past year (age 15)'), so age at diagnosis is 'not reported'. Complement was normal at 7.5 years, suppressed during flares at ages 8–11, and normal or elevated at ages 12–14; recorded as time-specific rows, not as a contradiction. Checklist judgements: 'mucosal ulcers have not been a feature ... at any point in her life' was applied as excluding oral and genital ulcers but not the composite GI 'ulcers or inflammation' item; CNS involvement marked observed from the CSF white-cell elevation during a hospitalization 'for concern of meningitis' (no meningitis diagnosis is named); cytopenia (autoimmune) marked observed from pancytopenia/thrombocytopenia with positive anti-platelet antibodies, though the paper does not use the word autoimmune; elevated inflammatory markers (CRP/ESR) left not reported because only ferritin is reported, not CRP or ESR. Variant type 'nonsense' is from the authors' 'premature stop codon'. The paper states no functional assay was done; this is recorded in functional_evidence_statement. HPO IDs are given only where certain; others are null.
